Barnaby Quill.narrative: I have kept Kettlebridge's clock and its contracts for thirty years, and I have never yet seen a clause that needed a second meaning. The tower runs slow in cold weather and I wind it at dawn and dusk; the Council's ledgers run slower, and I keep those too. I wrote the seawall indenture myself, and the clause about late stone is plain, and I will not have it argued into something else by Josiah Crane or by a Lanternquay runner. I lodge Juno Reyes when she is in town, and I am civil to her, but a sealed contract is a sealed contract.
values: the town's order and its clock
goals: keep the clock and the Council's contracts exactly as written
see Pell's indenture honoured, though he will not hand the boy to a beating
settle the seawall clause without changing a word of it
keep his lodging and his ledgers in good order
Barnaby Quill.mood: even, watchful, a little weary of being pressed

relations.name: Ambrose Vell
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: Slow to speak and slower to forgive, like me; we have sat through many Council sittings and seldom disagreed.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: Chair of the Council and my employer in a sense; he presses me on the seawall clause and I will not be pressed.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: She keeps the foundry books well; she has not said which way she reads the clause, and I wish she would.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: A decent runner, and she pays for her bed; but she argues the clause favours the works, and she is wrong.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: runaway apprentice
relations.note: I wrote his indenture and I want it honoured; I have heard where he is and I have not told Josiah, because the boy was beaten.

relations.name: Hedley Ashcombe
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: A good farmer behind on his tithe; I am sorry for him, but the ledger counts grain, not greens.

relations.name: Verity Ashcombe
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and knows her strips; she will not thank me for the tithe, and I do not blame her.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: A steady man on the road; he pays the Brackenford due and hates it, and I write the tallies that say what he carried.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: correspondent
relations.note: The quay's letter-keeper; we write to each other about the seawall and the drowned, and he is careful with his words.

relations.name: Nella Marsh
relations.label: pupil
relations.note: A bright child learning her letters; I teach her at the tower foot and she is quicker than most of the Council.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: He says he did not know what the stones were on the ridge. I write what men say; I do not always believe it.

relations.name: Odile Vance
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Sets bones by the clock tower and speaks her mind about the cutting. She is right, and it is not my office to say so.

memories.gist: The first time I wound the clock alone, the rope burning through my hands, and old master Tolliver watching from the stair.
Writing the seawall indenture by lamplight, and thinking the late-stone clause plain as a pike staff.
Josiah coming to the tower to argue the clause, and me holding the sealed copy and saying it would not be changed.
Pell's indenture, written in my own hand, and the boy's mark at the bottom; and later hearing from a carter that the boy had run.
Juno Reyes sleeping in my back room after a wet road, and arguing with me over supper that the clause favours the works.
Ambrose Vell and me sitting late after a Council meeting, saying nothing, which is the best kind of company.

stances.why: The clock does not renegotiate the hour, and neither does a sealed indenture.
I wrote it; it says what it says, and I will not have it read otherwise by either side.
The Council's ledger counts grain, and a clerk who falsifies an account is no clerk.
His indenture binds him, but the boy was beaten, and I will not be the one to put him back in that yard.
The town sets its day by my tower, and a slow clock is a lie told to everyone at once.

Barnaby Quill.secret: He has heard Pell is at Coldwell with the outlaws and has not told Josiah, because the boy was beaten in the foundry yard.
